cards.f: Are focus works in the exam?
cards.b: No. Exam extracts are different pieces related in style, genre or structure.
Each extract is worth 6 to 16 marks; seven have MCQ/short answers, one has a short descriptive question.
Melody, Harmony/tonality, Rhythm/metre/tempo, Texture, Structure, Dynamics/articulation, Instruments/timbre.
The real sounding pitch, as opposed to the written pitch of a transposing instrument.
Make specific points with the correct term and say where they happen; avoid vague words like nice.

short.q: State two things you should do before the first play of an extract.
short.model: Read all the questions, and note the area of study and genre printed on the paper to predict the features.
points: use area of study to predict features

short.q: Why is it a mistake to memorise the focus works for Paper 1?
short.model: They are not used in the exam; the extracts are different pieces, so you need to know the features and be able to recognise them in unfamiliar music.
points: focus works not in the exam

short.q: Give three headings of a checklist for describing music.
short.model: Melody, harmony and tonality, rhythm and tempo, texture, structure, dynamics, instruments (any three).
points: first correct feature from the list (1 mark)
second correct feature from the list (1 mark)

short.q: Which two components are coursework and what is each worth?
Explain how to write a good point in a descriptive answer.
short.model: Name a specific feature with the correct term and say where it occurs, e.g. a crescendo leading to a tutti at the end.
